No held instrument extends it beyond September 30, 1988.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register machine text of Executive Order 12462 (49 FR 6473, PDF pages 9-10 of the 1984-02-22 issue; sha256 5cedb5a9...), headed Executive Order 12462 of February 17, 1984, President’s Advisory Committee on Mediation and Conciliation, matching the census register row (1984-02-17). Text and inventory: eight machine scopes cover sections 1 through 4(b) to the signature, one of them (sec3-c) holding sections 3(c) and 4(a) and one (sec3-b-dup2) being section 4(b); I confirm the inventory. All clauses belong to one advisory committee. Ending: the Committee's own term. Section 4(b) as restated by Executive Order 12617 ends it no later than September 30, 1988 unless sooner extended; the four restatements (12497, 12533, 12579, 12617) are held and no later extension is held (Executive Order 12610 of 1987 does not list the Committee). The date is the first end, ahead of the later revocation by Executive Order 12692 (effective 1989-09-30). Disclosed limit: no held source shows an extension past, or an end before, September 30, 1988. Original grade: Federal Register machine text.

savings.reason: Executive Order 12692 contains no wording that preserves the order establishing the President's Advisory Committee on Mediation and Conciliation: its section 1 continues other committees, its section 2 reassigns Federal Advisory Committee Act functions only for those other committees, and its section 3 revokes this order without exception. Reports or other work already done are completed acts; nothing continues the Commission.
